Meteorology

moderate turbulence

Turbulence that causes changes in altitude and/or attitude but aircraft remains in control; occupants may feel strain against seat belts.

Questions and answers

What is moderate turbulence?

In this glossary, moderate turbulence refers to: Turbulence that causes changes in altitude and/or attitude but aircraft remains in control; occupants may feel strain against seat belts.

How is moderate turbulence used in aviation?

In aviation communication, this term appears in contexts such as: "Experiencing moderate turbulence at FL350, requesting lower altitude."

Why does moderate turbulence matter in aviation?

moderate turbulence matters because it supports clear communication in Meteorology contexts for Pilots, Air Traffic Controllers, and Cabin Crew. It also connects to aviation training and exam language such as ICAO Level 4, ICAO Level 5, ICAO Level 6, and EASA FCL.055.

moderate turbulence is mainly used by Pilots, Air Traffic Controllers, and Cabin Crew.
